| [LIT-096](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md) | What Is It Like to Be a Bat? | Nagel (1974), [DOI-10.2307/2183914](https://doi.org/10.2307/2183914). | [LIT-122](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-122.md) v2 | The Representation of Time and Change in Mechanics | Belot (2005), DOI-10.1016/B978-044451560-5/50005-1. For theories with ideal existence, uniqueness and a dynamical time-translation group, time is three intertwined ℝ-actions (on spacetime, on the symplectic space of solutions, and on the isomorphic space of initial data), and change is a slicing-indexed family of functions on those spaces. Singular dynamics, gauge freedom and time-dependence each damage this picture in a repairable way. Spatially compact vacuum GR breaks it, because the reduced Hamiltonian vanishes (h ≡ 0) and there is only one canonical isomorphism between the reduced spaces. That is the problem of time. It is not an artefact of the 3+1 split, it does not show change to be illusory, and it is absent from asymptotically flat GR and from artificially generally covariant theories. A parameterized "geometric time", such as CMC, restores change and, in the CMC case, a time-dependent Hamiltonian flow. | Active — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-118](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-118.md)); worth reading as the careful technical-philosophical statement of what the problem of time is and is not in classical GR. He extends Floridi's informational structural realism with one thesis: empirically equivalent but structurally different models (wave/particle/field descriptions, superstring dualities, AdS/CFT holography, equivalent programs in digital physics) have equal ontological standing. Since nothing stands "behind" them with a privileged configuration, the descriptions, i.e. information, are themselves fundamental, and theoretical objects exist as ontological primitives. There is no formal argument, and the physics is presented by assertion, with several errors. | Rejected — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-096](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-096.md)); not worth a reader's time on this topic. It misreports its source (Floridi, [LIT-152](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-152.md)) on the points it builds on, and it states contested or wrong physics as established. Its one novel move, reading dualities as equal-status alternatives rather than underdetermination, is asserted, not argued, and is done properly in the duality literature ([LIT-113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-113.md), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md)). |
